source: Royal University of Agriculture student technical report on Alfalfa cultivation (Medicago sativa), referencing international agronomy sources (Utah State University, FAO, and others)
text:
This Royal University of Agriculture (RUA) student technical report covers alfalfa (Medicago sativa), a perennial forage legume grown for animal feed rather than for direct human food use, distinguishing it from the grain/vegetable pulses covered elsewhere in this batch. The report is compiled primarily from international agronomy references (citing Utah State University Extension and FAO material among its sources) applied to a Cambodian student-research context rather than being MAFF-published extension material, so it should be read as a more academic/general-agronomy source than the batch's farmer-extension leaflets.

Alfalfa is described as a long-lived perennial (multiple years of production from a single planting, unlike the annual pulses elsewhere in this batch) valued for high-protein forage yield and, like other legumes in this batch, for biological nitrogen fixation via root-nodule rhizobia that reduces the crop's own nitrogen fertilizer requirement and can benefit following crops in rotation.
